info.title: Render Public API
info.description: Manage everything about your Render services

tags.name: Audit Logs
tags.description:
[Audit Logs](https://render.com/docs/audit-logs) allow you to retrieve audit logs for workspaces and organizations.
These logs provide a trail of actions and changes made to your resources.

tags.name: Blueprints
tags.description:
[Blueprints](https://render.com/docs/infrastructure-as-code) allow you to define your resources in a `render.yaml` file and automatically sync changes to your Render services.
The API gives control over how your Blueprints are used to create and manage resources.

tags.name: Custom Domains
tags.description: [Custom Domains](https://render.com/docs/custom-domains) allow you to associate domain names with your Render services.

tags.name: Dedicated IPs
tags.description: [Dedicated IPs](https://render.com/docs/dedicated-ips) provide static, outbound IP addresses for your Render services.

tags.name: Deploys
tags.description:
[Deploys](https://render.com/docs/deploys) are the process of updating your service with new code or configuration.
These endpoints allow you to retrieve data on the deploys of your services
as well as trigger new deploys and rollbacks. Most changes to your service
will require a new deploy to take effect.

To create and manage services, use the `Services` endpoints.

tags.name: Disks
tags.description: [Disks](https://render.com/docs/disks) allow you to attach persistent storage to your services.

tags.name: Environment Groups
tags.description: Collections of environment variables and secret files that can be shared between multiple services

tags.name: Events
tags.description: View events for a service, postgres or key value

tags.name: Key Value
tags.description: [Key Value](https://render.com/docs/key-value) allows you to interact with your Render Key Value instances.

tags.name: Logs
tags.description:
[Logs](https://render.com/docs/logging) allow you to retrieve logs for your services, Postgres databases, and redis instances.
You can query for logs or subscribe to logs in real-time via a websocket.

tags.name: Maintenance
tags.description: The `Maintenance` endpoints allow you to retrieve the latest maintenance runs for your Render services. You can also reschedule maintenance or trigger it to start immediately.

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description: The `Metrics` endpoints allow you to retrieve metrics for your services, Postgres databases, and redis instances.

tags.name: Notification Settings
tags.description:
[Notification Settings](https://render.com/docs/notifications) allow you to configure which notifications you want to receive, and
where you will receive them.

tags.name: One-Off Jobs
tags.description: [One-off jobs](https://render.com/docs/one-off-jobs) are standalone tasks that run to completion using the most recent successful build of an existing service.

tags.name: Postgres
tags.description:
[Postgres](https://render.com/docs/postgresql) endpoints enable you to interact with your Render Postgres databases.
You can manage databases, exports, recoveries, and failovers.

tags.name: Projects & Environments
tags.description: Collections of services and other resources organized by environment (staging, production, etc.)

tags.name: Registry Credentials
tags.description: [Registry Credentials](https://render.com/docs/deploying-an-image#credentials-for-private-images) allow you to manage credentials for private Docker images.

tags.name: Sandboxes
tags.description: Sandboxes are ephemeral, isolated compute environments for running code, executing commands, and transferring files. Sandboxes are in public beta.

tags.name: Services
tags.description: [Services](https://render.com/docs/service-types) allow you to manage your web services, private services, background workers, cron jobs, and static sites.

tags.name: Services - Cron Jobs
tags.description: [Cron Jobs](https://render.com/docs/cronjobs) allow you to interact with runs of your cron jobs.

tags.name: Services - Headers
tags.description: Use HTTP headers to inject response headers in static site responses. You can also use wildcards like /path/* to add headers to responses for all matching request paths.

tags.name: Services - Routes
tags.description: Add Redirect or Rewrite Rules to modify requests to your site without writing code. You can use URL parameters to capture path segments, and wildcards to redirect everything under a given path.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: The `User` endpoints allow you to retrieve information about the authenticated user

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: The `Workspaces` endpoints supply more information about the workspaces that your API key has access to. This category was previously called `Owners`, as reflected by endpoint paths.

tags.name: Build Sources
tags.description: Manage shared build sources for builds and images.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: [Webhooks](https://render.com/docs/webhooks) allow you to manage your Render webhook configuration.

tags.name: Workflows
tags.description: Create and manage [Render Workflows](https://render.com/docs/workflows) services.

tags.name: Workflow Tasks
tags.description: Run and manage tasks as part of [Render Workflows](https://render.com/docs/workflows).

tags.name: Workflow Flows
tags.description: Run and inspect durable flows as part of [Render Workflows](https://render.com/docs/workflows).

tags.name: Redis (Deprecated)
tags.description: [Redis](https://render.com/docs/redis) allows you to interact with your Render Redis instances. This API is deprecated in favor of the Key Value API.

post.description:
Validate a `render.yaml` Blueprint file without creating or modifying any resources. This endpoint checks the syntax and structure of the Blueprint, validates that all required fields are present, and returns a plan indicating the resources that would be created.

Requests to this endpoint use `Content-Type: multipart/form-data`. The request body (including the Blueprint file) cannot exceed 10MB in size.

ownerId.description: The ID of the workspace to validate against. Obtain your workspace ID from its Settings page in the Render Dashboard.

file.description: The render.yaml file to validate, as a binary file.

valid.description: If `true`, the Blueprint validated successfully. If `false`, at least one validation error occurred.

path.description: The path to the field with the error (e.g., `services[0].plan`)

line.description: The line number in the YAML file (1-indexed)

column.description: The column number in the YAML file (1-indexed)

errors.description: A list of validation errors. Only present if `valid` is `false`.

plan.description: A summary of the resources that would be created as part of the Blueprint. Only present if `valid` is `true`.

services.description: The names of services that would be created as part of the Blueprint.

databases.description: The names of Render Postgres databases that would be created as part of the Blueprint.

keyValue.description: The names of Render Key Value instances that would be created as part of the Blueprint.

envGroups.description: The names of environment groups that would be created as part of the Blueprint.

workflows.description: The names of workflows that would be created as part of the Blueprint.

totalActions.description: The total number of actions that would be performed by the Blueprint. In addition to created resources, this includes modifications to individual configuration fields.

post.description: Trigger a deploy for the service with the provided ID.

buildId.description: The ID of the build to deploy. Cannot be combined with `commitId`, `imageUrl`, or `deployMode`.

clearCache.description: If `clear`, Render clears the service's build cache before deploying. This can be useful if you're experiencing issues with your build.

commitId.description:
The SHA of a specific Git commit to deploy for a service. Defaults to the latest commit on the service's connected branch. Cannot be combined with `buildId`, `imageUrl`, or `deployMode: deploy_only`.

Note that deploying a specific commit with this endpoint does not disable autodeploys for the service.

You can toggle autodeploys for your service with the [Update service](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-service) endpoint or in the Render Dashboard.

Not supported for cron jobs.

imageUrl.description:
The URL of the image to deploy for an image-backed service. Cannot be combined with `buildId`, `commitId`, or `deployMode: deploy_only`.

The host, repository, and image name all must match the currently configured image for the service.

deployMode.description:
Deployment mode controlling build and deploy behavior.

Defaults to `build_and_deploy` when not specified.

**Validation:** `deployMode` cannot be combined with `buildId`. `deploy_only` cannot be combined with `commitId`, `imageUrl`, or `clearCache`.

post.description:
Create a preview instance for an image-backed service. The preview uses the settings of the base service (referenced by `serviceId`), except settings overridden via provided parameters.

View all active previews from your service's Previews tab in the Render Dashboard.

Note that you can't create previews for Git-backed services using the Render API.

imagePath.description: Must be either a full URL or the relative path to an image. If a relative path, Render uses the base service's image URL as its root. For example, if the base service's image URL is `docker.io/library/nginx:latest`, then valid values are: `docker.io/library/nginx:<any tag or SHA>`, `library/nginx:<any tag or SHA>`, or `nginx:<any tag or SHA>`. Note that the path must match (only the tag or SHA can vary).

name.description: A name for the service preview instance. If not specified, Render generates the name using the base service's name and the specified tag or SHA.

plan.description: The compute plan to use. Legacy variants (`*_legacy`) identify grandfathered plans no longer offered for new services. Note that base services on any paid compute plan can't create preview instances with the `free` plan.
plan.title: plan

buildSourceId.description: The ID of the Build Source the service builds and deploys from, if any. A git-backed Build Source must be in the same region as the service.

autoDeploy.description:
Deprecated: use `autoDeployTrigger` instead. You can't set both `autoDeploy` and `autoDeployTrigger` in the same request.

- `yes` is equivalent to `autoDeployTrigger: commit`.
- `no` is equivalent to `autoDeployTrigger: off`.
autoDeploy.title: autoDeploy

autoDeployTrigger.description:
Controls autodeploy behavior.

- `commit`: Deploy each time a commit is pushed to the service's linked branch.
- `checksPass`: Deploy each time a commit is pushed to the linked branch, but only after the commit's CI checks pass.
- `off`: Disable autodeploys.

get.description:
List logs matching the provided filters. Logs are paginated by start and end timestamps.
There are more logs to fetch if `hasMore` is true in the response. Provide the `nextStartTime`
and `nextEndTime` timestamps as the `startTime` and `endTime` query parameters to fetch the next page of logs.

You can query for logs across multiple resources, but all resources must be in the same region and belong to the same owner.

parameters.name: ownerId
parameters.description: The ID of the workspace to return logs for

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description: Epoch/Unix timestamp of start of time range to return. Defaults to `now() - 1 hour`.

parameters.name: endTime
parameters.description: Epoch/Unix timestamp of end of time range to return. Defaults to `now()`.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description:
The direction to query logs for. Backward will return most recent logs first.
Forward will start with the oldest logs in the time range.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Filter logs by their resource. A resource is the id of a server, cronjob, job, postgres, redis, workflow, or sandbox group. Required unless `project` is provided.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The ID of a project to return logs for. The query covers the project's services, cron jobs, Postgres databases, and Key Value instances. Combine with `resource` to narrow the query to specific resources in the project.

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: The ID of an environment in the project to return logs for. Requires `project`.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region to return logs for, such as `oregon`. Requires `project`. Required when the project's or environment's resources are in more than one region.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: Filter logs by the instance they were emitted from. An instance is the id of a specific running server.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Filter request logs by their host. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.

parameters.name: statusCode
parameters.description: Filter request logs by their status code. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: Filter request logs by their requests method. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: Filter logs by their task(s)

parameters.name: taskRun
parameters.description: Filter logs by their task run id(s)

parameters.name: sandbox
parameters.description: Filter logs by sandbox ID.

parameters.name: build
parameters.description: Filter logs by build ID, such as a service build or a sandbox image build.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Filter logs by their severity level. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter logs by their type. Types include `app` for application logs, `request` for request logs, and `build` for build logs. You can find the full set of types available for a query by using the `GET /logs/values` endpoint.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Filter by the text of the logs. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Filter request logs by their path. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).

- First move or delete all contained services and other resources.
- Delete the project in the [Render Dashboard](https://dashboard.render.com).

- Delete the environment in the [Render Dashboard](https://dashboard.render.com).

post.description:
Create a build source that can be linked to one or more
services in the same workspace.

Exactly one of `git` or `image` must be set:
- `git`: the build source is git-backed. The code is built in
   the requested `region` (defaults to `oregon`).
- `image`: the build source is image-backed. It points at an
  existing image in an external registry; no build is performed.

`envVars`, `secretFiles`, and `envGroupIds` set the build-time
environment and are only valid for `git` sources; the request fails
if any are provided with `image`.

buildFilter.description: Glob patterns matched against files changed by a commit. When set, a commit only triggers a build when at least one changed file matches `paths` and none match `ignoredPaths`. Useful for monorepos where a single repo backs many services.

dockerContext.description: Directory passed to `docker build` as the build context, relative to the repository root. Only valid for the `docker` runtime. Defaults to ".".

runtime.description: Build runtime for the build source. Static sites are not supported for build sources.

generateValue.description: If true, Render generates a strong random value for this environment variable on creation. Cannot be combined with `value`.

secretFiles.description: Secret files for the build source's build. Only valid for `git` sources.

envGroupIds.description: IDs of env groups to link to the build source. Only valid for `git` sources; env groups must belong to the same workspace and must not be scoped to an environment.

ownerId.description: ID of the workspace this build source belongs to.

projectId.description: ID of the project this build source is scoped to, if any.

unset fields are left unchanged.

underlying identity:

post.description:
Start a new build of the build source at the current HEAD of its
branch, even if an up-to-date build already exists.

By default, all services linked to the build source with autodeploy enabled
will be deployed. Use `deploy.serviceScope` to override this and choose specific
linked services.

Updating a build source or its build-time environment (env vars,
secret files, env groups) with the REST API does not build it. Call
this endpoint after those changes to build them.

Only `git` build sources can be built.

clearCache.description: If `clear`, Render clears the build source's build cache before building. This can be useful if you're experiencing issues with your build.

serviceScope.description:
Which linked services the build deploys to:

- `autodeploy_only`: every linked service with autodeploy on, including services set to deploy after CI checks pass. Services with autodeploy off do not get a deploy.
- `none`: no services. The build runs and deploys nothing.
- `custom`: the linked services in `serviceIds`, regardless of their autodeploy setting.

serviceIds.description: IDs of the linked services to deploy to. Required when `serviceScope` is `custom`, and not allowed with the other scopes. You must be authorized to trigger a deploy for each service that you include in this list.

buildRun.description: The Render build run that produced this build. Present when the build source is currently build-based. Mutually exclusive with `image`.

image.description: Present when the build source is currently image-based. Mutually exclusive with `buildRun`.

deploys.description: The deploys that the build started, one for each service.

reason.description:
Why the service did not get a deploy:

- `suspended`: the service is suspended.
- `deploys_shut_off`: Render has temporarily paused deploys for the service's plan tier.

skippedServices.description: Services in `deploy.serviceScope` that did not get a deploy, with the reason for each. The build still runs for the other services. For `autodeploy_only`, suspended services are not listed.

get.description:
Establishes a unidirectional event stream. The server sends events as lines
formatted per the SSE spec. Clients should set `Accept: text/event-stream`
and keep the connection open.

The server sends a `task.completed` event whenever a requested task run reaches
any terminal state (`completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`).
The `status` field of the payload indicates which state was reached.

The server automatically closes the stream in the following cases:

- All requested task runs have reached a terminal state.
- The stream has not sent any events for 30 minutes.

For tasks with a timeout higher than 30 minutes, waiting clients should fall back
to polling with the [Retrieve task run](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/gettaskrun)
endpoint.

parameters.name: taskRunIds
parameters.description: Filter to a subset of task run IDs.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: Must be `text/event-stream`.

schema.description:
Stream of SSE frames. Each event may include `id`, `event`, `data`,
and optional `retry`. Frames are separated by a blank line.

post.description: Create a sandbox and return its initial state. The sandbox might still be starting when the response is returned. To use a saved snapshot or custom image, provide `snapshotId`, `snapshotName`, `buildId`, or `buildName`.

schema.description: The sandbox to create, including its compute plan, network policy, and optional source build or snapshot.

ownerId.description: The ID of the workspace the sandbox belongs to.

allOf.description: The ID of the sandbox group.

sandboxGroupId.description: The ID of the sandbox group to create the sandbox in. Defaults to the workspace's default group.

name.description: A label for the sandbox, such as `my-agent`, up to 64 characters. Names do not have to be unique; use the sandbox ID to identify a specific sandbox. Must not start with `sbx-`.

networkPolicy.description: The outbound traffic policy to apply to the sandbox. Provide `type` or its deprecated alias `default`. If both are provided, they must match.

allOf.description: How Render handles outbound traffic from the sandbox. The `allow-list` policy requires `rules`.

type.description: How Render handles outbound traffic from the sandbox. The `allow-list` policy requires `rules`. Required unless `default` is provided. If `networkPolicy` is omitted, defaults to `allow-all`, or to the source sandbox's policy when creating a sandbox from a snapshot.

allOf.description: How Render handles outbound traffic from the sandbox. The `allow-list` policy requires `rules`.

default.description: A deprecated alias for `type`. Use `type` instead.

items.description: A destination that sandboxes can access when the network policy is `allow-list`.

domain.description: The hostname this rule allows, up to 253 characters. Matching is exact: `foo.local` does not match `api.foo.local`. Use a separate rule or `*.foo.local` for subdomains. A wildcard is allowed only as the leftmost label.

protocol.description: The protocol allowed for this destination. Defaults to `https`. The `allow-list` policy blocks outbound traffic that uses other protocols.

rules.description: Destinations the sandbox may reach, required when the policy is `allow-list` and rejected otherwise. Each domain may be listed once.

anyOf.description: The compute plan for the sandbox. The `starter`, `standard`, and `pro` plans are deprecated.

plan.description: The compute plan for the sandbox. See `sandboxPlan` for known values.

timeoutSeconds.description:
The maximum time the sandbox can run continuously, in seconds. The sandbox terminates when this time elapses. If the sandbox is suspended and later resumed, this timeout restarts.

Use 0 to disable the runtime timeout. Positive values must be between 60 and 2592000 (30 days). Defaults to 86400, or to the source sandbox's runtime timeout when creating a sandbox from a snapshot.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: The number of seconds of inactivity before Render suspends the sandbox. Use 0 to disable automatic idle suspension. Positive values must be between 300 and 86400. Defaults to 900, or to the source sandbox's idle timeout when creating a sandbox from a snapshot.

env.description: The environment variables to set when creating the sandbox.

allOf.description: The ID of the sandbox snapshot.

snapshotId.description: The ID of the snapshot to create the sandbox from instead of the base image. The snapshot must be `available` and belong to the same sandbox group. For a `runtime` snapshot, `plan` must match the snapshot's plan. The new sandbox inherits the source sandbox's network policy, timeout, and idle timeout. Provide `networkPolicy`, `timeoutSeconds`, or `idleTimeoutSeconds` to override these settings.

allOf.description: A case-sensitive name for snapshots in a sandbox group, up to 64 characters. Must not start with `snp-`. Multiple snapshots can share a name. When creating a sandbox by snapshot name, Render uses the most recently created snapshot with that name that is `available` and unexpired.

snapshotName.description: The name of the snapshot to create the sandbox from. Uses the most recently created snapshot with this name in the sandbox group that is `available` and unexpired. Cannot be combined with `snapshotId`. The same restore requirements as `snapshotId` apply.

allOf.description: The ID of the sandbox build.

buildId.description: The ID of the build to create the sandbox from instead of the base image. The build must have succeeded and belong to the same sandbox group. Cannot be combined with `buildName`, `snapshotId`, or `snapshotName`.

buildName.description: The name of the build to create the sandbox from instead of the base image. Uses the newest successful build with this name in the sandbox group. Cannot be combined with `buildId`, `snapshotId`, or `snapshotName`.

201.description: The sandbox was created. Returns its initial state.

items.description: A destination that sandboxes can access when the network policy is `allow-list`.

domain.description: The hostname this rule allows, up to 253 characters. Matching is exact: `foo.local` does not match `api.foo.local`. Use a separate rule or `*.foo.local` for subdomains. A wildcard is allowed only as the leftmost label.

protocol.description: The protocol allowed for this destination. Defaults to `https`. The `allow-list` policy blocks outbound traffic that uses other protocols.

rules.description: Destinations the sandbox may reach, present when `type` is `allow-list` and absent otherwise. Each domain may be listed once.

region.description: The Render region where the sandbox runs.

timeoutSeconds.description: The maximum time the sandbox can run continuously, in seconds. The sandbox terminates when this time elapses. If the sandbox is suspended and later resumed, this timeout restarts. A value of 0 disables the runtime timeout.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: The number of seconds of inactivity before Render suspends the sandbox. A value of 0 disables automatic idle suspension.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the sandbox was created, in ISO 8601 format.

terminatedAt.description: The timestamp when the sandbox was terminated, in ISO 8601 format. Null if the sandbox has not been terminated.

400.description:
The request is invalid.

- `invalid_snapshot_name`: `snapshotName` is malformed.
- Both `snapshotId` and `snapshotName` are provided. No error code is returned.
- `invalid_sandbox_name`: `name` exceeds 64 characters or starts with `sbx-`.
- `sandbox_group_limit_reached`: The workspace has no default sandbox group and has reached its sandbox group limit.
- `invalid_sandbox_plan`: The plan is not supported. The error message lists accepted plans.
- `invalid_timeout_seconds`: A nonzero `timeoutSeconds` is outside the range of 60 to the workspace's maximum, which defaults to 2592000 (30 days).

parameters.name: ownerId
parameters.description: The ID of the workspace the sandbox belongs to. If provided, it must match the sandbox's workspace. If omitted, Render determines the workspace from the sandbox ID.

schema.description: The settings for the sandbox snapshot to capture.

kind.description: The state to capture in the snapshot. Defaults to `runtime`.

allOf.description: The state to capture. A `filesystem` snapshot captures the writable filesystem and can be restored to any plan. A `runtime` snapshot also captures memory and CPU state and must be restored to the source sandbox plan.

name.description: A case-sensitive name for snapshots in a sandbox group, up to 64 characters. Must not start with `snp-`. Multiple snapshots can share a name. When creating a sandbox by snapshot name, Render uses the most recently created snapshot with that name that is `available` and unexpired.

ttlSeconds.description: The snapshot's lifetime after its last use, in seconds. Creating a sandbox from this snapshot resets its remaining lifetime to this duration. Use 0 to keep the snapshot until you delete it. Defaults to Render's snapshot lifetime. Cannot be combined with `expiresAt`.

expiresAt.description: The expiration timestamp, in ISO 8601 format. Deprecated; use `ttlSeconds` instead. Must be in the future. Render sets the snapshot lifetime to the duration between the request and this timestamp.

202.description: The snapshot capture was accepted. Returns the snapshot in `creating` status.

schema.description: A saved filesystem or runtime state that can be used to create another sandbox.

id.description: The ID of the sandbox snapshot.

sandboxGroupId.description: The ID of the sandbox group.

allOf.description: The ID of the sandbox.

sourceSandboxId.description: The ID of the sandbox this snapshot was captured from, recorded for reference.

allOf.description: A case-sensitive name for snapshots in a sandbox group, up to 64 characters. Must not start with `snp-`. Multiple snapshots can share a name. When creating a sandbox by snapshot name, Render uses the most recently created snapshot with that name that is `available` and unexpired.

name.description: The name assigned when the snapshot was created. Cannot be changed. Null if no name was provided.

kind.description: The state to capture. A `filesystem` snapshot captures the writable filesystem and can be restored to any plan. A `runtime` snapshot also captures memory and CPU state and must be restored to the source sandbox plan.

status.description: The snapshot's current status.

anyOf.description: The compute plan for the sandbox. The `starter`, `standard`, and `pro` plans are deprecated.

plan.description: The source sandbox's compute plan when the snapshot was captured. See `sandboxPlan` for known values.

requestedAt.description: The timestamp when the snapshot was requested, in ISO 8601 format.

capturedAt.description: The timestamp when capture completed, in ISO 8601 format. Null until the snapshot is `available`.

expiresAt.description: The timestamp after which the snapshot can no longer be retrieved or restored, in ISO 8601 format. Each time you create a sandbox from this snapshot, Render resets its expiration to `ttlSeconds` seconds after that use. For snapshots with no expiration (`ttlSeconds: 0`), this is `9999-12-31T23:59:59Z`.

ttlSeconds.description: The snapshot's lifetime after its last use, in seconds. A value of 0 means the snapshot does not expire. If omitted, Render's default snapshot lifetime applies.

sizeBytes.description: The size of the snapshot, in bytes. Null until the snapshot is `available`.

error.description: The reason the snapshot failed. Null unless its status is `failed`.

post.description:
Restore a retained credential version, including its routing settings, injection settings, and secret value, as a new current version. Requires an admin.

The new version has a higher ID, records who restored it and when, and identifies the source in `restoredFromVersionId`. Its fingerprint matches the source version. Render retains the current configuration and the three distinct prior configurations most recently active. Removing an older configuration also removes all versions that refer to it.

The response confirms the configuration was saved. It does not confirm that credential injection is active for a particular sandbox.

These endpoints do not return secret values.

schema.description: The retained credential version to restore.

versionId.description: The ID of a retained credential version to restore as a new current version.

schema.description:
A credential configured for injection into matching outbound HTTPS requests from sandboxes in one sandbox group. Each credential stores its own secret value. These endpoints do not return secret values, including to admins.

Credential injection supports HTTPS requests on port 443. Avoid overlapping credential configurations for the same hostname. Multiple matching credentials are not combined.

id.description: The case-sensitive ID you assign to the credential, unique within its sandbox group. Use only letters, numbers, periods, underscores, tildes, and hyphens. The names `.` and `..` and IDs starting with `rnd-` are reserved.

domain.description: The destination hostname to match for credential injection. Must be a public DNS hostname. Render normalizes it to lowercase and matches it exactly. IP addresses, ports, wildcards, and local or internal hostnames are not supported.

version.description: Metadata for a credential version. These endpoints do not return secret values.

id.description: The ID of the credential version. Each new version receives a higher ID, including versions created by a restore.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when this credential version was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updatedBy.description: The ID of the authenticated identity that created this credential version.

fingerprint.description: A fingerprint of the routing settings, injection settings, and secret value. Matching fingerprints identify equivalent credential configurations within the same sandbox group. Fingerprints cannot be compared across groups.

restoredFromVersionId.description: The ID of the credential version restored to create this version. Omitted for versions created by a create or update request.

enabled.description: Whether this credential is enabled for injection.

methods.description: The HTTP methods to match for credential injection. Supported methods are GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and OPTIONS, normalized to uppercase. An empty list matches any method.

paths.description: The request path patterns to match for credential injection. Each pattern must match the entire absolute path. Use `*` for one nonempty path segment or `**` for one or more segments. Wildcards must occupy whole segments. For example, `/a/*` matches `/a/b`, and `/a/**` also matches `/a/b/c`. Neither matches `/a`. Patterns do not support query strings, fragments, or escaping. Request query strings do not affect matching. An empty list matches any path.

injection.description: Settings for injecting the secret value into matching outbound HTTPS requests.

type.description: How Render adds the credential to a matching request. For `basic`, the value after applying `template` must have the form `username:password`. Do not provide `name`.

name.description: The header, cookie, or query parameter to set. Required for `header`, `cookie`, and `query`. Headers that control routing or connection behavior cannot be used.

template.description: A template containing 1–5 occurrences of `${SECRET}`, such as `Bearer ${SECRET}`. Render replaces each occurrence with the secret value. Omit to use the secret value without a template.

post.summary: Mint a connect token for a sandbox file transfer
post.description:
Create a short-lived connect token for a file upload or download. Transfer the file directly to or from the URL in the response, using the token as the bearer token. The token authorizes only the specified sandbox, operation, and path. Its expiration time is returned in `expiresAt`.

Use `application/octet-stream` for a single file or `application/x-tar` for a directory archive. For gzip compression, also set `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Directory downloads return `application/x-tar` with `Content-Encoding: gzip`.

parameters.name: path

The file or directory path the token authorizes. For archive uploads, this is the directory to extract into. For downloads, it is the file or directory to retrieve.

Relative paths are resolved from the image's `WORKDIR`, or the home directory if no `WORKDIR` is set. Use `.` for that working directory. Absolute paths are resolved from the sandbox filesystem root.

DeployMode.description:
Controls deployment behavior when triggering a deploy.

- `deploy_only`: Deploy the last successful build without rebuilding (minimizes downtime)
- `build_and_deploy`: Build new code and deploy it (default behavior when not specified)

**Note:** `deployMode` cannot be combined with `buildId`. `deploy_only` cannot be combined with
`commitId`, `imageUrl`, or `clearCache`, as those are build related fields.

name.description: The label set when the sandbox was created.

status.description: The sandbox's current status.

anyOf.description: The compute plan for the sandbox. The `starter`, `standard`, and `pro` plans are deprecated.

type.description: How Render handles outbound traffic from the sandbox. The `allow-list` policy requires `rules`.

allOf.description: How Render handles outbound traffic from the sandbox. The `allow-list` policy requires `rules`.

default.description: A deprecated alias for `type`, returned with the same value. Read `type` instead.

items.description: A destination that sandboxes can access when the network policy is `allow-list`.

protocol.description: The protocol allowed for this destination. Defaults to `https`. The `allow-list` policy blocks outbound traffic that uses other protocols.

rules.description: Destinations the sandbox may reach, present when `type` is `allow-list` and absent otherwise. Each domain may be listed once.

region.description: The Render region where the sandbox runs.

timeoutSeconds.description: The maximum time the sandbox can run continuously, in seconds. The sandbox terminates when this time elapses. If the sandbox is suspended and later resumed, this timeout restarts. A value of 0 disables the runtime timeout.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: The number of seconds of inactivity before Render suspends the sandbox. A value of 0 disables automatic idle suspension.

terminatedAt.description: The timestamp when the sandbox was terminated, in ISO 8601 format. Null if the sandbox has not been terminated.

execution.description: A record of a command run or file transfer in a sandbox. `startedAt` records when the connect token was created. id.description: The ID of the sandbox execution.

type.description: Whether the execution is a command run or a file transfer.

operation.description: The command run or file transfer operation authorized by the connect token.

command.description: The command run in the sandbox, or the target path for a file transfer. Command text may be redacted or truncated. Omitted if you do not have permission to view execution commands.

userId.description: The ID of the user the execution token was created for.

startedAt.description: The timestamp when the execution token was created, in ISO 8601 format.

stoppedAt.description: The timestamp when the execution stopped, in ISO 8601 format. Omitted until a result is available.

exitCode.description: The execution exit code. Omitted until a result is available.

id.description: The ID of the sandbox snapshot.

allOf.description: The ID of the sandbox.

sourceSandboxId.description: The ID of the sandbox this snapshot was captured from, recorded for reference.

allOf.description: A case-sensitive name for snapshots in a sandbox group, up to 64 characters. Must not start with `snp-`. Multiple snapshots can share a name. When creating a sandbox by snapshot name, Render uses the most recently created snapshot with that name that is `available` and unexpired.

name.description: The name assigned when the snapshot was created. Cannot be changed. Null if no name was provided.

kind.description: The state to capture. A `filesystem` snapshot captures the writable filesystem and can be restored to any plan. A `runtime` snapshot also captures memory and CPU state and must be restored to the source sandbox plan.

status.description: The snapshot's current status.

anyOf.description: The compute plan for the sandbox. The `starter`, `standard`, and `pro` plans are deprecated.

plan.description: The source sandbox's compute plan when the snapshot was captured. See `sandboxPlan` for known values.

requestedAt.description: The timestamp when the snapshot was requested, in ISO 8601 format.

capturedAt.description: The timestamp when capture completed, in ISO 8601 format. Null until the snapshot is `available`.

expiresAt.description: The timestamp after which the snapshot can no longer be retrieved or restored, in ISO 8601 format. Each time you create a sandbox from this snapshot, Render resets its expiration to `ttlSeconds` seconds after that use. For snapshots with no expiration (`ttlSeconds: 0`), this is `9999-12-31T23:59:59Z`.

ttlSeconds.description: The snapshot's lifetime after its last use, in seconds. A value of 0 means the snapshot does not expire. If omitted, Render's default snapshot lifetime applies.

sizeBytes.description: The size of the snapshot, in bytes. Null until the snapshot is `available`.

error.description: The reason the snapshot failed. Null unless its status is `failed`.
